LESSON: SIGN READING 2.4.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: CLASS READER

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Sign Reading 2.4.1 Intensive sign Reading: Class Reader
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 2.4.1 Intensive sign Reading: Class Reader, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: where I learned it - what I want to know - what I learned (K-W- W-L) chart to visualise what has been learned. 1. Why should we not judge a book by its cover?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 2.4.1 Intensive sign Reading: Class Reader together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn : Learners develop the skill of organising their own learning as they build on their learning experiences through

analysis of the setting and research on the author.

● Critical thinking: Learners develop research skills as they explore the links between different events through tasks like creating graphic

organisers that cultivate high-order thinking skills.

● Problem-solving: Learners develop the skill of open mindedness and creativity as they conduct research online to obtain more

information about the author and the setting of the story.

Values:
● Unity: is enhanced as the learner develops skills for working in harmony with others while participating in group and pair work.

Link to other Subjects:

The learner relates the skill of intensive sign reading to their reading of class readers in Kiswahili.
